**Implementation Plan - NYC Farmer Markets App (spooky-themed SwiftUI)**

**Problem Statement:**

Every tab opens the same detail sheet, and closing it returns to the originating tab.

**Requirements:**
- Data source: Socrata dataset 8vwk-6iz2, endpoint https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/8vwk-6iz2.json. Verified fields, all strings: year, marketname, borough, streetaddress, community_district, latitude, longitude, daysoperation, hoursoperations, accepts_ebt, open_year_round, nyc_dept_of_health_cooking. Coordinates must be parsed to Double and may be missing. There is no unique ID, so build a stable ID from name + address. Normalize borough (trim, fall back to "Unknown"). Check the full row count and borough value consistency during Task 2.
- Tab 1 Markets: searchable list grouped by borough (fixed order: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Bronx, Staten Island, then others). Search filters name, address, and borough, case-insensitive, and hides empty sections.
- Tab 2 Map: pins for markets with coordinates, camera centered on NYC. Selecting a pin shows a bottom card with the name and a "More info" button. That button opens the shared detail sheet. Closing returns to the map.
- Tab 3 Favorites: list of favorited markets sorted by name. Tap shows details. Swipe deletes the favorite. There is no Edit button. Spooky empty state.
- Detail view: a sheet shared by all tabs, driven by a single .sheet(item:) bound to MarketStore.selectedMarket. It has a Close button and shows all fields, an "Go to Map" button, and a favorite toggle (ghost icon) in the toolbar. Closing returns to the tab the user came from.
- Favorites are stored locally as a set of market IDs (UserDefaults or small JSON). If a favorited market is missing from the dataset, skip it in the list and keep its ID stored.
- Offline: cache the last successful fetch to disk. On launch, load the cache first, then refresh from the network. On failure, keep showing the cache with an "Offline, showing saved data" banner. If there is no cache, show an error state with Retry. Support pull to refresh.
- Theming: use the palette #C7D93D (primary/accent), #98A62E (secondary), #525919 (deep, text on light and dark-mode background), #E6F28D (highlight/cards/selected), #F2F2F2 (light surface). Colors are defined IN CODE in a single place (AppPalette) with semantic tokens and light/dark variants. Changing the base values in that one place recolors the whole app. Views must use only semantic tokens and AppIcon, never literal Color(...) or hex values, or raw SF Symbol names. The light tints on light surfaces have low contrast, so text on light uses deep #525919, and dark mode uses #F2F2F2/#E6F28D text. Don't claim full WCAG compliance, since manual testing with assistive technologies is still needed.
- Icons: an AppIcon enum registry maps each role (tab Markets, tab Map, tab Favorites, favorite on/off, map pin, EBT, year-round, hours, location, close) to either spooky SF Symbols (moon.stars.fill, eye.fill, cloud.fog.fill, flame.fill, sparkles, moon.fill) or custom-drawn SVG template assets (ghost for favorites, bat for map pin, pumpkin for market), added to Assets.xcassets as template images so they take the theme tint. Render it to a 1024x1024 PNG and install it in the AppIcon set in Assets.xcassets for supported platforms (iOS, macOS, visionOS). Add the olive as a named theme token (appIconBackground). Keep the SVG source in the project so the user can swap in original artwork later. It is a flat image with the olive background baked in. Build and check there are no asset catalog warnings. The look on a device cannot be verified.

**Architecture:**
- MarketStore (@Observable): markets, state (idle/loading/loaded/error), isShowingCachedData, selectedMarket, refresh().
- FavoritesStore (@Observable): Set<String> of IDs, isFavorite/toggle/remove, persisted.
- Both injected through the SwiftUI environment from NYCFarmerMarketsApp.
- MarketService (URLSession, injectable URL/session), MarketCache (atomic JSON file).
- Views: RootTabView, MarketListView, MarketMapView, FavoritesView, MarketDetailView, and theme types in a Theme folder.
- New .swift files in NYCFarmerMarkets/ should be picked up automatically (file-system-synchronized groups). Verify at build time, and edit the project file only if needed.

Task 1: Theme and icon system
- Objective: Build the palette, semantic tokens, icon registry, and custom assets with a preview.
- Guidance: Create Theme/AppPalette.swift (five base hex values defined once, semantic tokens such as accent, accentSecondary, textOnLight, background, card, cardSelected, separator, appIconBackground, with light/dark variants) and Theme/AppIcon.swift. Draw SVG ghost, bat, and pumpkin template assets in Assets.xcassets. Apply global tint and tab/navigation bar appearance. Add a ThemePreviewView (SwiftUI preview) showing all tokens and icons in light and dark.
- Tests: Contrast-ratio checks for the text/background token pairs. Every AppIcon case resolves to an existing symbol or asset.
- Demo: The preview shows the palette and icons, and changing a base hex in one place recolors it.

Task 2: Model and network service
- Objective: Fetch and decode markets.
- Guidance: Create Market (Identifiable, Codable, Hashable) with a DTO decode that maps the string fields, parses coordinates to optional Doubles, builds a stable id, and normalizes borough. Create MarketService with async throws fetchMarkets() and an injectable URL/session. Check the live data (row count and borough values).
- Tests (Swift Testing, NYCFarmerMarketsTests): Decode a fixture, missing coordinates, ID stability, and service behavior using a mocked URLProtocol.
- Demo: Tests pass, and a live check logs the market count.

Task 3: Cache layer and MarketStore
- Objective: Add offline-first loading.
- Guidance: MarketCache with atomic JSON read/write. MarketStore loads the cache first, then the network, writes the cache on success, and keeps the cache on failure. Expose state, isShowingCachedData, and refresh().
- Tests: Cache round trip, network success updates the cache, failure with cache falls back, failure with no cache gives an error state.
- Demo: Launch and see the market count, turn on Airplane Mode, relaunch, and the data still shows.

Task 4: Tabs and Markets list
- Objective: Add the searchable list grouped by borough.
- Guidance: Replace ContentView with a TabView and wire up the stores in NYCFarmerMarketsApp. MarketListView is a NavigationStack with sections per borough (secondary-colored headers), .searchable, .refreshable, a loading indicator, error with Retry, the offline banner, and rows showing name, address, and day (with a ghost indicator for favorites once Task 6 lands). - Tests: Unit tests for the grouping and filtering function (order, case-insensitivity, empty results).
- Demo: Browse and search the grouped list, pull to refresh, and test offline.

- Guidance: MarketDetailView in a NavigationStack with a Close button, all fields, and an "Go to Map" button. The sheet is driven by .sheet(item:) at the root bound to MarketStore.selectedMarket. Closing clears the selection and returns to the active tab. Add presentationDetents and accessibility labels. Use themed cards.
- Tests: A UI test that taps a row, sees the detail, taps Close, and sees the list again.
- Demo: Tapping a row opens the sheet, and Close returns to the list.

Add the ghost toggle in the detail toolbar with a state-dependent accessibility label (Add to favorites / Remove from favorites) and a symbol effect or haptic. Add favorite indicators to the Markets list rows. Inject the store through the environment.
- Tests: Toggle on and off, persistence across a new store instance, and unknown IDs ignored when resolving favorites to markets.
- Demo: Favorite a market in the sheet, relaunch, and the ghost is still filled.

Task 7: Favorites tab
- Objective: List favorites with swipe to delete.
- Guidance: FavoritesView lists favorited markets sorted by name, with borough, address, and day. Tapping a row opens the shared sheet, and Close returns to the Favorites tab. Swipe to delete removes the favorite (no Edit button). A market missing from the dataset is skipped but its ID stays stored. The empty state reads "No haunts yet. Favorite a market to summon it here." Add the third tab with the AppIcon.
- Tests: A unit test for the resolved, sorted list. A UI test that favorites a market, sees it in the tab, swipes to delete, and sees the empty state.
- Demo: Favorite two markets, see them in tab 3, swipe one away, and unfavorite the other from the sheet.

Task 8: Map tab
- Objective: Show the map and wire it to the same sheet.
- Guidance: MarketMapView uses SwiftUI Map with Marker/Annotation (custom bat or pumpkin pin from AppIcon, tinted with accent) for markets that have coordinates, camera centered on NYC, and a distinct style for favorites. Selecting a pin shows a bottom card (highlight background) with the name and a "More info" button, which sets selectedMarket and opens the shared sheet. Closing returns to the map with the pin still selected.
- Tests: A UI test that taps a pin or the card, opens the detail, and closes it.
- Demo: Tap a pin to see the name, tap More info to see the detail, and Close returns to the map.

Task 9: App icon, polish, and verification
- Objective: Install the app icon, finish polish, and verify.
- Guidance: Draw the carrot SVG (see Requirements), render the 1024x1024 PNG, and install it in the AppIcon set; add the appIconBackground token. Add Dynamic Type support, empty and error states, light/dark mode, and iPad/Mac layout checks (sheet sizing). Remove leftover template code. Run a grep check that no view uses literal colors, hex values, or raw SF Symbol names outside Theme/. Run the full build and tests, and confirm there are no asset catalog warnings. Clean up temporary files.
- Demo: A full run-through of all three tabs on the simulator, with the new app icon showing.
